ai.description: *Cnemaspis wicksi* is a small gecko reaching 45 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Distinctive features include a keeled venter and granular scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis wicksi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles on the flanks, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis wicksi* is endemic to the Andaman Islands, where it primarily inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found on tree trunks and rocky surfaces.
ai.behavior: *Cnemaspis wicksi* is a strictly nocturnal gecko that remains hidden in rock crevices during the day to avoid predators and extreme heat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis wicksi* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis wicksi* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, where it is found at low elevations.
